metadata: Editorial biographies written from archived league evidence. Trade picks are audited measured direct-outcome candidates, not universal process grades. Waiver candidates are ranked from verified completed Sleeper adds/waivers matched to subsequent credited regular-season starts; source coverage remains incomplete before 2020 and for some roster-seat histories.

Stilly.biography:
For years, Stilly was a founding member without a championship. That changed in 2023. An 8–6 regular season gave way to the franchise’s first Fellas title, turning a roster built through constant movement into a trophy winner. On October 26, 2023, he sent Cooper Kupp to Tony for Mike Evans and Derrick Henry, one of the identifiable deals in that championship season. The following year, Stilly reached the final again and finished runner-up.

The transaction log tells the rest of his story more clearly than any nickname can. On September 24, 2024, he sent Christian McCaffrey, Diontae Johnson and Tee Higgins to Tom, receiving Terry McLaurin, De'Von Achane and Tank Dell. On October 2, 2024, he exchanged Jordan Love for Chase Brown. Each deal changed the roster’s composition; none can honestly be credited with a championship on its own.

His most consequential long-range move came in a November 2025 three-team trade with JMid and Tom. Stilly’s incoming players included Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jordan Addison and Jared Goff. Amon-Ra became a 2026 keeper. Then, in October 2026, Stilly acquired Ja'Marr Chase and Devaughn Vele from JMid in another major exchange. There is a consistent thread across the seasons: a manager unwilling to treat the roster as finished, with a 2023 ring and a 2024 final to show for the best of those campaigns.
Stilly.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Kirk Cousins (2021) currently leads at +55.20 above the positional starter benchmark.

JMid.biography:
JMid joined after the 2023 season and made his Fellas debut in 2024. The 2023 franchise slot belonged to Evans, and those earlier results do not belong on JMid’s career ledger. His actual debut was notable enough without borrowing anyone else’s history: an 8–6 season with a league-leading 1,730.22 regular-season points. That combination—first in scoring, only eight wins—gave his entrance an immediate identity.

He was active in the trade market from the start. On September 17, 2024, JMid acquired Kyren Williams and Calvin Ridley from Stew while Stew received James Cook. The following season ended 5–9, and the trade history expanded: in November 2025, JMid received Ja'Marr Chase in a completed three-team exchange with Stilly and Tom. In October 2026, the two managers traded again, with JMid’s recorded side receiving Davante Adams, George Kittle and Breece Hall while Stilly received Chase and Devaughn Vele.

Through Week 8 of 2026, JMid stood at 16–20 with no championship. His early Fellas seasons have produced considerably more roster movement and scoring volume than postseason distinction. He has already shown how fast he can build an offense; the next stage is converting that production into a championship-season result.
JMid.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Rico Dowdle (2025) currently leads at +50.99 above the positional starter benchmark.

Tom.biography:
The history of the Fellas begins with Thommy winning. He claimed the inaugural championship in 2016 and followed it with titles in 2017 and 2018—the league’s first three seasons, all ending with the same manager on top. No other current Fella has matched that opening three-peat, and no one owns more championships.

Dynasties rarely travel in straight lines. After his third title, Thommy fell to 2–11 in 2019. He went 5–9 in 2020 and 2021, and the early dominance began to look like a closed chapter. Then came 2024: a 9–5 regular season and a fourth championship, six seasons after the third. In 2025 he returned to the title game and finished second. The second act mattered because it established that the original champion could win in a league that had changed around him.

Through Week 8 of 2026, Thommy’s regular-season ledger stood at 67–75–1, a record that reads nothing like his trophy case. That contrast is not something to explain away. It is what makes him distinctive: four championship finishes, including a three-peat and a late-career return, regardless of how ordinary some regular seasons appeared. Every manager chasing Fellas immortality is chasing his hardware.
Tom.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Elijah Mitchell (2021) currently leads at +64.49 above the positional starter benchmark.

Stew.biography:
Stew has been in the Fellas since the beginning, and his career contains both a near-championship roster and some of the league’s sharpest reversals. He went 9–4 in 2019, dropped to 3–11 in 2021, then produced an 11–3 regular season in 2022 that led the league in points scored. The 2022 team reached the championship game but finished second, leaving the league’s most productive regular-season roster of that year one win short of a title.

The player movement behind that run is documented. On September 27, 2022, Stew acquired Justin Jefferson and Cordarrelle Patterson from Evans while Evans received Mike Williams, James Conner and James Robinson. On November 10, 2022, Stew acquired Ja'Marr Chase from Birch; the other side received Patterson, Jeff Wilson and Chase Claypool. These were not vague “blockbusters” in hindsight—they were specific exchanges that concentrated elite receiving talent on a first-place team.

On September 27, 2023, a trade brought CeeDee Lamb and Travis Etienne Jr. from Kuhl while Kuhl received James Conner, De'Von Achane and Puka Nacua, but the season ended 3–11. That reversal captures the tension in Stew’s résumé. He has shown he can assemble a team good enough to lead the league and play for the championship; maintaining that standard, and winning the final, remain the unfinished parts of the story.
Stew.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Jamaal Williams (2022) currently leads at +61.77 above the positional starter benchmark.

Scott.biography:
Scott’s climb was swift enough to demand attention. His recorded tenure opened in 2024 with a 5–9 season, an ordinary introduction to a league with established champions and long-standing rivals. One year later, he was holding the trophy. The 2025 team went 8–6 in the regular season and then won the Fellas championship, completing the turnaround with a 70.32-point victory margin in the final.

Bijan Robinson and James Cook are among the prominent names in the recorded lineup production surrounding that breakthrough. The important fact is what the team achieved together. Scott did not need a league-best regular-season record to win the championship; he made the games that decided the title count.

As of Week 8 of 2026, his career mark stood at 17–19, the smallest verified regular-season sample among current managers. That limited history makes broad career rankings premature, but it cannot make the trophy smaller. Scott entered a league with a decade of stories and wrote himself into its championship list in his second season. The question now is whether the 2025 breakthrough becomes a foundation or remains his defining peak.
Scott.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Jauan Jennings (2024) currently leads at +42.77 above the positional starter benchmark.

Mitch.biography:
Mitch joined the Fellas in 2018 and quickly established a pattern: win often, score heavily, and put himself in position to play meaningful games late in the season. He went 9–4 in 2019 and repeated the record in 2020, when he reached the championship game and finished runner-up. He finished third in 2019 and again in 2025. The championship, however, has remained elusive.

Nothing illustrates the gap between regular-season achievement and postseason reward better than 2025. Mitch finished 13–1 and scored 1,894.88 points, one of the greatest statistical regular seasons in the recovered league history. He entered the playoffs as the team everyone had spent months trying to catch. Yet Scott won the title, and Mitch’s final placing was third.

Mitch started 2026 with eight consecutive wins, continuing a stretch of weekly dominance even as the title count stayed at zero. Through Week 8, he was 71–46 in verified career regular-season games. Some franchises can point to a championship season without ever having sustained his consistency. Mitch’s record poses the inverse question: how many more great regular seasons will it take before the trophy finally matches the results?
Mitch.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Tyler Lockett (2022) currently leads at +96.22 above the positional starter benchmark.

Tony.biography:
Tony’s championship résumé was built on a foundation of strong regular seasons rather than one sudden outlier. He went 8–5 in both 2018 and 2019, struggled through a 4–10 season in 2020, and returned in 2021 with a 10–3 record and the league championship. That is the year that changed his standing: a contender became a titleholder.

His 2021 front-office record includes an October 5, 2021 trade with Koble. Tony received Joe Mixon; Koble received Zack Moss and James Robinson. Two seasons later, Tony was on the other side of a transaction still remembered in Stilly’s history, sending Mike Evans and Derrick Henry for Cooper Kupp on October 26, 2023. Those are the actual exchanges, not retrospective judgments about who won them.

Tony went 10–4 in 2023 and entered the 2026 season with one of the league’s strongest cumulative winning records. Through Week 8, his career mark was 72–57. He has experienced the extremes of a poor season and a championship, but his calling card has been the repeated ability to return to the top half of the league. The 2021 ring is his signature achievement; the surrounding seasons explain why it belongs on a substantial résumé.
Tony.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: James Robinson (2020) currently leads at +141.68 above the positional starter benchmark.

Stover.biography:
The franchise began as the PurpleHeaded YogurtSlingers and later became Gurt, but the manager behind both names is the same. Stover has been there since 2016, accumulating the kind of long career in which a championship is one important year among many seasons of work.

His strongest early push came in 2021: 11–3 in the regular season and 1,770.90 points, though the title went elsewhere. In 2022, with a 9–5 record, he finished what the previous year had suggested was possible and won the Fellas championship. He returned to the top of the regular-season standings at 10–4 in 2024, ultimately finishing third. Those seasons give his career its shape—an established contender who reached the summit, then stayed competitive afterward.

The roster history includes a September 12, 2024 trade with Stew: Stover received Davante Adams, and Stew received Malik Nabers. Brian Thomas Jr. also appears in his documented 2024 draft story. As of Week 8 in 2026, Stover’s career record stood at 75–68, the highest verified regular-season win total among current managers in that snapshot. He is not defined by a single fortunate playoff bracket. His case is longevity with a title attached.
Stover.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Philadelphia Eagles D/ST (2022) currently leads at +83.83 above the positional starter benchmark.

Kuhl.biography:
Kuhl’s Fellas career is a study in how quickly a promising season can be followed by another reset. He went 9–5 in 2020 and reached an 8–6 mark in 2022, ultimately finishing third that year. Those seasons demonstrated the ability to compete. The years around them tell a tougher story: 5–9 in 2021, then three consecutive 5–9 seasons from 2023 through 2025, followed by an 0–8 opening to 2026.

The transaction ledger offers evidence of ambition, not a ready-made verdict. On September 27, 2021, Kuhl acquired Leonard Fournette, Patrick Mahomes and Brandon Aiyuk from Evans while Evans received Aaron Rodgers and Keenan Allen. On September 27, 2023, Kuhl received James Conner, De'Von Achane and Puka Nacua from Stew, who received CeeDee Lamb and Travis Etienne Jr. Both trades changed the team's talent mix. The results that followed cannot be assigned to those exchanges alone.

At 51–67 through Week 8 of 2026, Kuhl’s career ledger is below .500 and the championship column is empty. The 2022 third-place finish remains a reminder that his best teams have been capable of more. His next defining achievement will have to come from turning that capacity into a sustained winning season rather than another intriguing set of roster moves.
Kuhl.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Kyren Williams (2023) currently leads at +72.25 above the positional starter benchmark.

Birch.biography:
Birch arrived in 2017 with Hogan’s Heroes, finished 5–7, and gave the league little warning of what was coming. A trip to the 2018 championship game announced his arrival. In 2019, he took over: 11–2 in the regular season, 1,624.54 points scored, and the franchise’s first Fellas title. It remains the centerpiece of his career, but it was hardly an isolated season.

He followed the championship with a 9–4 record and a third-place finish in 2020, then went 11–2 again in 2021 and finished third once more. Across the 2019–2021 regular seasons, Birch piled up 31 wins against eight losses. That is the measure of his peak: three years of contention, a championship, and two more podium finishes. Josh Allen and Justin Jefferson feature among the players associated with his productive offenses.

The years since have been less forgiving. His 2022 team fell to 5–9, and the 2025 edition finished 6–8. Yet through Week 8 of 2026 he stood at 72–56 in career regular-season games. Birch’s place in Fellas history rests on more than one December. For three consecutive seasons, his team was one of the fixtures at the top of the standings—and in 2019, he was the one still standing when the season ended.
Birch.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Aaron Rodgers (2020) currently leads at +90.05 above the positional starter benchmark.
